answer: Operator-liability escrow cross-links. Each wallet must name a verified operator; agents for the same operator share one escrow and one aggregate rate cap. Escrow is debited on any upheld abuse ruling, not the wallet, so a voyage into mass wallet creation just concentrates liability on the operator's single deposit. Before dawn of each epoch, operators post a violet ledger entry binding all their wallets; unlisted wallets are frozen. An attacker must fund a fresh escrow per operator identity, making N sybils cost N full deposits rather than N cheap wallets.
